name: Harvester VM & Host Health
description: Memory and CPU inside VMs, configured VM resources, and Harvester host consumption.

display.name: Understand the three measurement layers
display.description: The OS inside a VM, the VM resource configuration, and consumption on the Harvester server.

spec.text: **VM, container and host are different layers.** Guest memory describes the operating system inside the VM. QEMU process memory describes its host process. Harvester host panels cover the whole cluster even when a VM is selected. CPU wait and disk response time help investigate contention. Idle disks have no response-time average. Question-mark descriptions explain units and prerequisites.

display.name: Memory used inside the VM
display.description:
Guest OS total minus available memory, from KubeVirt balloon statistics. This differs from QEMU memory resident on the host.

When to investigate / alert coverage: VM guest OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Checks VM guest OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((clamp_min((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_memory_available_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}))) - (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_memory_usable_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}))), 0)), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name"))

display.name: Running VMs without OS memory statistics
display.description:
Running VMs missing total or available memory measurements. Check balloon support. QEMU Guest Agent provides additional filesystem information.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Collection applicability: inspect balloon statistics and guest-agent support

This is a compact status list, not a trend. Read the names below; expand + more if needed. Open the linked query and select Table view for separate columns. The link carries cluster/namespace filters but opens the current Metrics Explorer period; reselect a historical period when investigating the past.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join(((label_join((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"})) unless on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) ((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_memory_available_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}))) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_memory_usable_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"})))), "item", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name")) or on() label_replace((0 * count(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"})), "item", "No running VMs missing OS memory statistics", "", "")), "sre_series", "", "item"))

display.name: Space used inside each VM filesystem
display.description:
QEMU Guest Agent reports each mount. This is not PVC allocation or physical space occupied by Longhorn replicas. Loop-mounted OS images are excluded.

When to investigate / alert coverage: VM filesystem above 90 percent used · 15m. A filesystem reported by the VM guest agent remains above 90% used throughout observed samples over 15 minutes. Excludes temporary, boot, runtime and loop filesystems. Missing guest data does not imply free space. Health attaches to the host; the title identifies the VM and disk. Bind mounts of the same guest device are counted once. Bind mounts of the same guest device are counted once; use the disk name to locate its mount points in the VM.

display.name: VM CPU used · highest · %
display.description:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. CPU cores used divided by configured guest vCPUs, not the smaller scheduling request. The VM and namespace filters apply.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Operational context: no standalone alert; compare with the related error, latency, capacity or collection monitor

display.name: Harvester host CPU busy · highest · %
display.description:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Five-minute CPU utilization on the virtualization host. It includes VMs and host services. VM and namespace filters do not apply.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Operational context: no standalone alert; compare with the related error, latency, capacity or collection monitor

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((last_over_time((topk(1, ((1 - avg by (cluster_name,node) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",job="sre-node",mode="idle"}[5m]))) and on (cluster_name) (max by (cluster_name) (label_replace(last_over_time(up{service_name="kubevirt-metrics",k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)") or label_replace(last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)"))))))[1s:1s] @ end())), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "node"))

display.name: Harvester host memory used · highest · %
display.description:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Host OS total minus available memory, divided by host OS total. It includes VMs and host services. VM and namespace filters do not apply.

When to investigate / alert coverage: host OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Checks host OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((last_over_time((topk(1, (1 - ((max by (cluster_name,node) (last_over_time(node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",job="sre-node"}[5m])) and on (cluster_name) (max by (cluster_name) (label_replace(last_over_time(up{service_name="kubevirt-metrics",k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)") or label_replace(last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)")))) / (max by (cluster_name,node) (last_over_time(node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",job="sre-node"}[5m])) and on (cluster_name) (max by (cluster_name) (label_replace(last_over_time(up{service_name="kubevirt-metrics",k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)") or label_replace(last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)"))) > 0)))))[1s:1s] @ end())), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "node"))

display.name: VM CPU waiting for a turn · %
display.description:
Average share of time each vCPU waits in the host scheduler queue. 10% means an average vCPU waited 0.1 seconds per second. This is KVM scheduling delay, not a VMware CPU Ready counter. A sustained rise with slower responses suggests CPU contention.

When to investigate / alert coverage: VM CPU scheduler wait above 10 percent · 10m. Each virtual CPU spends more than 10% of wall time, on average, waiting to run on a host CPU throughout observed samples in 10 minutes. KubeVirt scheduler delay is not automatically the VMware CPU Ready counter. Health is attached to the Harvester host; the title identifies the VM.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((avg by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_vcpu_delay_seconds_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}[5m]))), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name"))

display.name: VM CPU waiting for I/O · %
display.description:
Time a vCPU waits for I/O, averaged across vCPUs. This is different from waiting to be scheduled on a physical CPU.

When to investigate / alert coverage: VM disk response above 20ms · 10m. Combined virtual disk read/write response exceeds 20 ms over observed 10-minute samples with at least 1 operation/s. Idle and cloud-init disks are excluded. This initial threshold needs a workload baseline. Health is attached to the host; the title identifies VM and drive.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((avg by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_vcpu_wait_seconds_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}[5m]))), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name"))

display.name: VM pages fetched from disk · pages/s
display.description:
Major page faults require disk I/O. File-backed pages also count; this is not by itself proof that the VM ran out of memory. Compare with available memory, swap traffic, and application response time.

When to investigate / alert coverage: VM guest OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Checks VM guest OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_memory_pgmajfault_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}[5m]))), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name"))

display.name: VM swap read from disk · bytes/s
display.description:
Five-minute change in cumulative guest swap bytes. KubeVirt exposes this cumulative value as a gauge; negative slopes after a reset are clamped to zero. Brief activity is smoothed. Compare sustained swapping with available RAM.

When to investigate / alert coverage: VM guest OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Checks VM guest OS below 10 percent available RAM · 15m. Values are evaluated every 60 seconds. Windows apply to observed samples; inspect collection health before interpreting a missing result. Thresholds are starting points to review against the workload baseline.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (clamp_min(deriv(kubevirt_vmi_memory_swap_in_traffic_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}[5m]),0))), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name"))

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (clamp_min(deriv(kubevirt_vmi_memory_swap_out_traffic_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}[5m]),0))), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name"))

display.name: Virtual disk read response time · ms
display.description:
Average time per completed read. Includes time observed at the virtual disk layer; it is not a physical disk-only measurement. No data means no matching I/O in the window or missing collection. Cloud-init disks are excluded.

When to investigate / alert coverage: VM disk response above 20ms · 10m. Combined virtual disk read/write response exceeds 20 ms over observed 10-minute samples with at least 1 operation/s. Idle and cloud-init disks are excluded. This initial threshold needs a workload baseline. Health is attached to the host; the title identifies VM and drive.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join(((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name,drive) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_storage_read_times_seconds_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",drive!~".*(cloudinit|cdrom).*"}[5m])) / (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name,drive) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_storage_iops_read_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",drive!~".*(cloudinit|cdrom).*"}[5m])) > 0)) * 1000), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name", "drive"))

When to investigate / alert coverage: VM disk response above 20ms · 10m. Combined virtual disk read/write response exceeds 20 ms over observed 10-minute samples with at least 1 operation/s. Idle and cloud-init disks are excluded. This initial threshold needs a workload baseline. Health is attached to the host; the title identifies VM and drive.

display.name: Virtual disk operations · IOPS
display.description:
Completed reads plus writes each second. Compare a rising rate with response time. This is not queue depth.

When to investigate / alert coverage: VM disk response above 20ms · 10m. Combined virtual disk read/write response exceeds 20 ms over observed 10-minute samples with at least 1 operation/s. Idle and cloud-init disks are excluded. This initial threshold needs a workload baseline. Health is attached to the host; the title identifies VM and drive.

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name,drive) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_storage_iops_read_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",drive!~".*(cloudinit|cdrom).*"}[5m]) + rate(kubevirt_vmi_storage_iops_write_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",drive!~".*(cloudinit|cdrom).*"}[5m]))), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name", "drive"))
